content.text: Section 24 fully matches our preferred position, and no conflicting change-of-control trigger exists elsewhere.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 gives Customer an unqualified right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's consent (reasonableness standard running in our favour) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, with a cooperation obligation for successor administrative changes. Searches for "assign" and "change of control" across the document found no competing trigger — Section 9 termination contains only a standard mutual insolvency/general-assignment-for-creditors right, and Section 13.x confirms Customer may transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 permitted assignment. "Affiliate" (1.1) uses a conventional >50% control test, so the carve-out is not artificially narrow. No redline needed.
